question: If a woman accompanied by her husband requests MTP and avoids eye contact, answers with one-word responses, and defers all questions to her husband, the clinician should ask the husband to leave the room before continuing the consent consultation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is actually correct. Non-verbal signs of fear, avoidance of eye contact, one-word responses, and deference to an accompanying person are all red flags for coerced consent. Asking the companion to leave and assessing the woman privately is mandatory before proceeding.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. These are red flags for coerced or compromised consent. Requesting private consultation time with the woman alone is the single most important step in identifying coercion. A woman cannot give free, voluntary consent in the presence of a coercive partner.
